sec: MN figures, IF & the treatment split · p769

items.q: In the Ponticelli arm of the treatment chart, oral cyclophosphamide is given at 2 mg/kg on which months?
items.exp: Steroids are printed as 'On months 1,3,5' and oral cyclophosphamide (2 mg/kg) as 'On months 2,4,6', with the two brackets closing on 'Abrupt stop'. (Book p769)

items.q: Fill up: The bracket that groups the alternating steroid and cyclophosphamide months in the modified Ponticelli regimen ends with the instruction ______ stop.
items.exp: The brace beside the two drug lines is captioned 'Abrupt stop', i.e. the alternating cycles are stopped rather than tapered on this page. (Book p769)

items.q: Match each label of the membranous nephropathy diagram with what it points to — 1) Podocyte 2) Basement membrane 3) Deposits … A) Effaced foot processes B) Thickened C) Subepithelial, with spikes
items.exp: The diagram is labelled Podocyte with effaced foot processes, Thickened basement membrane, Subepithelial deposits and Spikes, and is captioned 'membranous nephropathy'. (Book p769)

items.q: The green capillary-loop photograph on this page carries which caption?
items.exp: The immunofluorescence photograph along the glomerular capillary loops is captioned 'IF in MN', sitting between the two light-microscopy photographs and the labelled diagram. (Book p769)

items.q: A 45-year-old with biopsy-proven MN has only trace proteinuria, normal albumin and no edema. Per the treatment chart's right-hand arm, the plan is:
opts: ACE inhibitor or ARB, salt restriction and 1 gm/kg/day protein
Modified Ponticelli regimen with steroids on months 1, 3 and 5
Rituximab, since MN always needs B-cell depletion
Renal biopsy repeat before any drug is started
items.exp: The 30% asymptomatic arm is managed with ACE(−)/ARBs, salt restriction and 1 gm/kg/day protein; the Ponticelli regimen and rituximab belong to the 70% who present with nephrotic syndrome. (Book p769)
